findings.problem: At large browser text sizes, the page 1 boxes overflow and are clipped. Spec section 4 lists "the browser's text size set to very large" as a check, and the builder's run did not cover it. `.cn-pair` stays two columns until a px breakpoint (`@media (max-width: 360px)`), while the text inside grows with `font-size: medium`. Measured with Page.setFontSizes: at Chrome's "Very large" (24 px) on desktop 1440/1280/700 wide, "Commentary" and "People’s words about the Bible" overflow their dashed box by 41 px and run through its border. On a 390 phone at 20 px they overflow by 19 px (26 px at 375). At 24 px they overflow by 61 px and are cut off at the screen edge, reading "Commentar" and "about the Bibl". The core word of the notice is clipped for exactly the readers who asked for big text. Screenshots: ...\craft\shots\P2-390x844-f24-p1.png (same as D-390x844-f24-dark-p1.png), P2-1440x900-f24-p1.png and P2-390x844-f20-p1.png.
findings.fix: Make the boxes stack with the text size, not the px width. For example `.cn-pair { grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 11em), 1fr)); }` and drop the 360px query. An em media query also works (`@media (max-width: 40em)`, since media-query em follows the browser default size). Add `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on `.cn-box b, .cn-box span` as a last resort. Re-check at 20 and 24 px default text at 390 and 1440.

findings.problem: At 200% zoom the notice's main words are hidden below a fold, with no sign there is more. It can help you understand the Bible, but it is not the Bible." is entirely below the fold, and the page looks finished, because the boxes end neatly at the divider. On page 2, "If anything here disagrees with the Bible, trust the Bible." is hidden. At 1366x768 zoomed to 200%, a very common laptop (C-zoom200-1366-p1/p2.png), the reading window is 183 px tall.
